first_impression.reaction: We're about 14 months out with no country picked, so a month-by-month list is exactly where we are. The intro goes straight to passports and legal papers instead of 'your dream day', and the destination track split is useful. I'll read on.

journey.quote: A year sounds like a long time until you count the things that cannot be rushed: a venue on your date, a gown made to measure, a passport renewal, legal papers for marrying overseas.
journey.reaction: Practical, no fluff. Passport and legal papers in the first line tells me they know what destination weddings involve.

journey.section: 12 months out: what to do first
journey.quote: If you are in Australia, lodging a new or renewal application generally cancels your current passport, so you cannot travel on it while you wait.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that. James's passport expires next year, so this is actually going to save us a headache.

journey.section: 12 months out: what to do first
journey.quote: Ask the same embassy whether you can get the CNI in Australia, because some local authorities only accept one issued in their country, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille.
journey.reaction: This is the legal side I worry about. Specific and linked to Smartraveller, so it feels checked.

journey.section: 10 to 11 months out: book the people who shape the day
journey.quote: Book your photographer and videographer. Look at full galleries from real weddings, not just highlights.
journey.reaction: The core lists are mostly what every checklist says. I skimmed these and only read the destination tracks properly.

journey.section: 10 to 11 months out: book the people who shape the day
journey.quote: Hold a block of rooms for guests close to the venue, with a release date agreed in writing.
journey.reaction: Release date in writing is a detail an insider would think of. Half our guests are flying in, so this matters.

journey.section: 10 to 11 months out: book the people who shape the day
journey.quote: Set up a wedding website or RSVP page where guests can find travel details as they firm up. [Wonderland Studio](/wonderland-studio) is one place to start.
journey.reaction: What is Wonderland Studio? Is that yours, a paid thing, a template? No idea from this.

journey.section: 10 to 11 months out: book the people who shape the day
journey.quote: For a destination wedding, send them earlier than you would for a local one, so guests can plan leave and travel.
journey.reaction: Earlier by how much? Our parents will ask for a number. This is the one place I wanted a clear answer.

journey.section: 8 to 9 months out: attire, accommodation and the celebrant
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is the one person who plans with you from start to finish, works in your time zone and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: This is the first time a planner has actually told me what 'end to end' means: one person, our time zone, fee in writing. That answers my question.

journey.section: 4 to 5 months out: when to send wedding invitations
journey.quote: For a destination wedding, send them early enough that guests can still book flights and leave.
journey.reaction: The heading promises 'when to send wedding invitations' and then doesn't give a timeframe. Feels like a dodge.

journey.quote: Confirm airport transfers for guests who have shared their flights.
journey.reaction: Getting my grandparents from the airport is our biggest worry. Is this on us, or does the Advisor do it? The list reads like we're doing it ourselves.

journey.quote: Some states and territories do not accept overseas marriage certificates for a name change.
journey.reaction: Didn't know this either. Honest, slightly annoying, but useful. This is the sort of trade-off I want told upfront.

journey.section: Plan the year with one person beside you
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor helps you decide it, as your single point of contact from the first idea, quoting in AUD and confirming inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD speaks to the currency surprises we're nervous about. Calm close, not pushy.

unanswered_questions: How many months before a destination wedding should save-the-dates and invitations actually go out?
Who books and confirms guest airport transfers if we use Wedded Concierge: us or the Advisor?
What is Wonderland Studio, and does it cost anything?
Roughly what does a destination wedding for 60 to 90 guests cost, even as a From AUD range? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Advisor fee structured, and does the Advisor use their own vendor network or whoever the venue suggests? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real wedding (venue, date) that followed this timeline? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would rather hand the logistics to one team, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=12-month-wedding-checklist&utm_content=secondary) plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Anywhere in the world' is the generic end-to-end line every planner uses. The later Advisor paragraph is far more convincing, so this one feels like filler.

turn_offs_found.quote: For a destination wedding, send them early enough that guests can still book flights and leave.
turn_offs_found.why: Vague where we need a number. Under a heading that promises the timing, it reads as avoiding the question.

would_share_with: James: the destination tracks and the passport points, since his passport is the one that needs renewing
My parents: the at-a-glance table, so they can see the year laid out without reading the whole thing

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [talk to Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=12-month-wedding-checklist&utm_content=closing) about your date and destination.
cta_reaction.why: Not yet. The tone is right and the 'fee in writing, quote in AUD, one person' points tick our boxes, but we don't have a destination and there's no real wedding or price range here. I'd save this, read a couple more posts and look for a real wedding first.

top_3_changes: Give actual timing for save-the-dates and invitations on a destination wedding. 'Send them earlier than you would for a local one' and 'early enough that guests can still book flights and leave' don't answer the heading.
Say who handles guest logistics like 'Confirm airport transfers for guests who have shared their flights' when you work with a Wedded Advisor, so the list doesn't read as all on us.
Lead with the specific Advisor promise ('works in your time zone and agrees the fee in writing') rather than the generic 'anywhere in the world' line, and explain what Wonderland Studio is.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (planner couple): skimmed core lists, read destination tracks, looked for guest logistics, legal certainty, accountability and costs
No invented brand facts; fees, vendor network, real weddings and Wonderland Studio listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Is there a sourced lead time for destination save-the-dates and invitations the writer can state, rather than 'earlier'?
Should the draft clarify which destination-track tasks a Wedded Advisor takes on (e.g. guest transfers, room blocks)?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for '12 month wedding checklist' during early research, no destination chosen, about 14 months out.
Business details and fee amounts are deferred and not penalised as must-fix.
Fast-mode read: intro, takeaways, destination tracks and CTAs read closely; core checklists, table and FAQ skimmed.
